LESSON: THE CELL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.1: The Cell
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Cell, part of Living Things and their Environment in Grade 8 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: What makes up plant and animal cells?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Cell in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Cell in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Cell in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Cell in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the role of cells in living things.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Cell in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope,

D. determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope,

   The Cell helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the role of cells in living things.

1. collaboratively prepare, mount, observe and draw plant cells as seen under a light microscope, (include a reminder on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Cell together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: the learner learns how to prepare, mount, observe, and draws plant cells as seen under a light microscope.

● Self-efficacy: the learner successfully prepares and observes specimens under the light microscope.

Values:
● Unity: the learner displays team spirit as they prepare, mount, observe, and draw plant cells as seen under a light microscope.

● Responsibility: the learner performs assigned roles as they observe, draw and label animal cells on permanent slides as seen

under the light microscope.

Link to other learning areas:

The concept of multiplication is learnt in Mathematics as the learner carries out multiplication of objective lens and eye piece

lens to get the magnification.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the structure of plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope,
2. describe the functions of components of cells seen under the light microscope,
3. compare plant and animal cells as observed under a light microscope,
4. determine the magnification of cells under the light microscope,
5. appreciate the role of cells in living things.

Remember the key question: What makes up plant and animal cells?
